subject: Urban Planning
title: The Right to the City
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Right to the City.

hook.text: Henri Lefebvre wrote in 1968 that cities belong to everyone who lives in them, not just those who own property.

buildup.text: The 'right to the city' means access to housing, transit, parks, and participation in decisions that shape neighborhoods.

discovery.text: Brazil enshrined it in law. The 2001 City Statute gave residents legal tools to fight displacement and speculation.

twist.text: In practice, enforcement is weak. Developers still displace favela residents for luxury projects across Brazil.

climax.text: The idea is spreading: Barcelona, Mexico City, and Montreal have all adopted right-to-the-city frameworks.

punchline.text: You live here. You have a right to shape here.

quiz.question: What does 'the right to the city' mean?
options: Property owners have the final say over urban development plans
All residents deserve access to housing, transit, parks, and planning decisions
Cities have the right to annex surrounding suburban areas
